acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHAT THE REPLAY CANNOT SHOW ABOUT THE LIVE SITE. Three named gaps plus a fourth the order did not name. (i) WAF TOKEN MINTING: aws-waf-token is minted by AWS WAF's browser challenge, executed as JavaScript in a real page. The replay Set-Cookies a random value; nothing about the challenge, its difficulty or its failure mode is exercised. If the live challenge fails or is served as an interstitial, the library classifies it CH-UNEXPECTED / SIG-WAF and fails explicitly -- which is the designed behaviour, and is also the untested path. (ii) COOKIE ROTATION TIMING: the whole reason the browser holds the session rather than a hand-rolled cookie header is that csrftoken and aws-waf-token rotate under the browser's feet. The replay rotates nothing across a session, so the library's reliance on the live context (probeSession via context.requestGet) is CORRECT BY DESIGN and UNMEASURED BY THIS PROOF. The first live run is the first test of whether a bundle persisted at time T is still assemblable at T+delta. (iii) AN EVICTION BY A PERSON: the injected eviction is a replay mode; a real one is Alyssa signing in. The 403 marker string 'concurrent sign in' is transcribed from ycharts_client.py's seat_evicted(), which is itself a reverse-engineered predicate -- if the vendor changes that wording, this library reports DISTURBED instead of EVICTED_HARD and reacquires zero times rather than N. That is a SINGLE STRING of shared dependency between this library and the market-data client, and it is the one place where both instruments would be wrong together. (iv) THE GAP THE ORDER DID NOT NAME, and it is the largest: THE SIGN-IN PAGE ITSELF IS UNMEASURED. All three supplied HARs are post-authentication; there is no login flow in any evidence available in this worktree (row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S2). The form action, the field names and the submit control are a Django-shaped MODEL, and the selector list the library tries is exactly the set that model satisfies. Related but separate: no real browser ran at all (row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S1), so arm (a)'s '5 of 5' is a statement about the library's mechanism, not about Chromium. (2) THE AWSCURRENT STATE OF ycharts/session/current AND WHAT IT IMPLIES. Measured 2026-09-10 via describe-secret: the secret EXISTS (arn ...:secret:ycharts/session/current-fxoD1K, LastChangedDate 1779374828) and VersionIdsToStages is NULL -- it has no AWSCURRENT version and no version of any kind. The brief's measurement re-grounds exactly. Four implications for the first live run. (a) getSession MUST treat absence as a VALUE: get-secret-value on a versionless secret raises ResourceNotFoundException, so a library that let that propagate would die before it ever reached a login. It returns {present:false, reason:'NO_AWSCURRENT_VERSION'} instead, and arm (a) proves that branch first. (b) The first live run necessarily takes the ACQUIRE path -- there is nothing to probe -- so the first live run is simultaneously the first exercise of the modelled login DOM, of the WAF challenge and of the lease. Those three unknowns land together, which is an argument for running it attended. (c) PutSecretValue on a secret with no versions CREATES version 1 and stages it AWSCURRENT; the role grants PutSecretValue on this ARN alone, so the mechanism is in place, but it has never been exercised against this secret and no version has ever existed. (d) The FENCE starts from nothing: persistSession compares against a stored fence of null and permits the first write unconditionally. That is correct for a first write and is the one lease state the difference control in arm (d) does not cover, because there is no prior holder to be fenced against. (3) WHAT OF THE BDAPI RUNNER WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED OVER, AND WHY. Five things, each a decision rather than an omission. (i) THE ENTIRE OTP APPARATUS -- getOtpCode and its adapter seam (graph/teams/relay), otpSent/otpEntered, the two-step delivery-screen handling, the 'Remember My Device' checkbox with its three fallback strategies, and the bd_DeviceRegistration device-trust inject/capture. Andrew's word is 'I do not believe they send OTP so dont need that part', and a code channel built on a belief about a vendor is worse than no channel: it would have to be tested against a challenge nobody has seen, and an untested credential-adjacent path is exactly where a quiet failure hides. It is replaced by an explicit refusal that NAMES the thing it will not do (CHALLENGE_ONE_TIME_CODE_UNSUPPORTED), so the day YCharts does send a code, the failure says so instead of timing out. (ii) THE OUTER MULTI-ATTEMPT LOGIN RETRY (BD_MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS with exponential backoff, up to 3 fresh browser contexts). BD's retry exists to survive a consumed-OTP race, which is the machinery that is gone; what remains would be repeated password submission against a vendor whose seat a human also uses. acquireSession is ONE attempt: a re-presented sign-in form after submit is an explicit AuthError, not a second password. The bound that DOES survive is on REACQUISITION AFTER AN EVICTION, which is a different event with a different cause. (iii) THE RESIDENTIAL PROXY AND ignoreHTTPSErrors. BD needed BrightData, then dropped it; carrying either forward would mean TLS interception on a path where the only measured requirement is normal TLS. Native egress and normal certificate validation. (iv) THE S3 DEBUG-SCREENSHOT CHANNEL (BD_DEBUG_SHOTS, masked fields, per-step PNGs to a debug prefix). It exists so an agent could watch a login it could not otherwise see, and it carries a standing ROE hazard -- pixels of a post-fill form. The IAM policy here grants no PutObject at all, so the channel is structurally absent rather than merely unused. What replaces it is a redacted structured record: cookie NAMES, a sha256 prefix, HTTP statuses, step states. (v) THE VISION PATH AS A HARD DEPENDENCY. The Kimi seam is preserved (opts.vision, and astn/kimi/api-key is granted) because the style Andrew named is DOM-first-with-vision-fallback, but classifyScreen reaches it only after DOM and signature checks, and the offline suite injects NO vision port -- replay_browser.js's screenshot() THROWS rather than stubbing, so the vision path cannot pass this suite without being exercised. It is present and honestly unproven, rather than present and falsely green. (4) FOR THE CVO'S ATTENTION, since it decides whether this cell's evidence supports FWD-4: the two ARMED rows W3-S1 and W3-S2 are disarmed only in the sense that the limitation is written where a reader stands. Nothing in this order can close them; closing either requires a live YCharts sign-in, which is Andrew's per-use word via 1.0.0_SA_CTO at L10.
